summary: @layer groups rules into layers with a set priority. A rule in a later layer beats a rule in an earlier layer, no matter how specific each selector is. Unlayered rules beat all layers.
notes: @layer base, components, utilities; sets the order. Later in the list means higher priority.
The third button matches #join-games in base and .btn in components. The id is more specific, but components is the higher layer, so .btn wins and the button is blue.
Inside a single layer, the normal rules still apply: specificity first, then source order.
pitfall: Forgetting that unlayered CSS beats every layer. A leftover rule outside the layers can override your whole layer setup, even with a weak selector.
